clue.text: Television programme rock drummer missed or …

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: A rock band's drummer failed to turn up, and the sentence trails off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' sits beside 'drummer' as a music genre, but it is the verb. The ellipsis runs the sentence on into 9 across. Midsomer Murders is a long-running British TV detective series set in English villages.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsomer Murders is a British television detective drama, so it is a television programme.

clue.text: Hebrew teacher inspires American hairstyling products

parts.note: Moses, the lawgiver who taught the Israelites
US = American

explanation.surface: A Hebrew teacher gives some American visitors the idea for hair products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspires' reads as giving an idea; it works in its literal Latin sense of breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousses are foams applied to hair to style and hold it.

clue.text: Trick hollow mirrors removed from fairground amusement

indicators.note: removed from says these letters are taken out of the fairground ride

parts.note: dodgems are the bumper cars at a fairground

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides scooped out, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: its outer letters M and S are used

explanation.surface: A deception: the hall of mirrors has been taken out of the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow mirrors' suggests a funfair hall of mirrors, but it means the shell of the word, MS, which comes off the end of DODGEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick or ruse used to evade something.

clue.text: Leaves behind away team's kit heading for stadium

parts.note: away = out, as in 'she is out'
a team's strip is its playing kit

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of STADIUM

parts.note: the first letter of STADIUM

explanation.surface: The away team's kit arrives at the stadium ahead of the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away team' looks like one football phrase, but the split falls between the two words. The 's belongs to the kit, not to a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip rivals is to leave them behind by going faster or further.

clue.text: Rascal escapes imminent death

parts.note: imminent = impending
an imp is a mischievous rascal; it is the part removed

explanation.surface: A rascal narrowly escapes death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a narrow escape; 'imminent death' looks like one phrase but 'imminent' is the fodder and 'death' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism in reverse: death is the close of a life, and books and films speak of a character's end in the same way.

clue.text: Batty woman arrived briefly upsetting centrepiece of musical medley

indicators.note: in a down answer, upsetting turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: Nora Batty is a character in the long-running BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the centrepiece of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: its middle letter I is used

explanation.surface: An eccentric woman arrives late and spoils the central number of a musical medley.
explanation.walkthrough: Nora Batty is the wrinkled-stockinged character from the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine. NORA plus CAM is reversed to MACARON, then the middle letter of musical is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni can mean a confused mixture or jumble, from the mixed Latin and vernacular of macaronic verse.

clue.text: Bank just ignores graduate

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out

parts.note: just = barely, as in 'just made it'
a Bachelor of Arts, the part removed

explanation.surface: A bank only just turns down a graduate's application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the lender turning down a graduate; it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym through the phrasal verb: you can bank on or count on a friend.

clue.text: Cautioned when playing, gets coaching

indicators.note: the letters of CAUTIONED are played about with

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A player booked during a match is sent off for extra coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a footballer shown a yellow card; 'playing' is the signal to rearrange 'cautioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaching is teaching or instruction, which is education.

clue.text: Cunning minor takes drug

parts.note: minor = slight, of little importance
E = ecstasy

explanation.surface: A crafty youngster starts taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' reads as a child, suiting 'cunning'; it is the adjective meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: the word survives mainly in 'sleight of hand', a conjuror's crafty skill.

clue.text: … saw by middle of June, day not specified

indicators.note: takes the central letters of JUNE

parts.note: the two central letters of JUNE
to see someone is to go out with them, so saw = dated

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: a drummer went missing, or was seen around mid-June on some unrecorded day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a proverb; here it is the past tense of seeing someone romantically. 'By' simply places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a letter or document with no date written on it leaves its day unspecified.

clue.text: University feeds craze concerning art, literature etc

indicators.note: to feed something in is to insert it

parts.note: a cult is a fad or craze
re = concerning, as in memo headers
U = university

explanation.surface: A university fuels a fashionable craze for the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'art, literature etc' sits at the end and describes the whole field rather than any single art.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture is the arts and intellectual achievement taken together.

clue.text: Bribe corrupt Western Europeans being seized

indicators.note: the letters of WESTERN are corrupted into a new order
the two Es are taken into the mix

parts.note: anagram fodder
E = European, twice

explanation.surface: A bribe offered to corrupt Western Europeans who are being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective describing the Europeans, and 'bribe' supports that reading; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or bribe that makes a deal more attractive.

clue.text: Go for Glaswegian group committing crimes?

definitions.meaning: the Scots verb for go, as a Glaswegian would say it

explanation.surface: A suggestion to join a Glasgow crime gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Glaswegian' flags a Scots word, and the crime group supplies the same letters as a straight noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use and a plain synonym: the Scots verb as in 'gang aft agley', and the ordinary noun for a criminal band.

clue.text: Offer Cambridge University loan previously

indicators.note: previously means earlier, so the loan comes first, before the university

parts.note: a sub is a small advance or loan
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A student is offered a loan by Cambridge University in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University suggests the English one; it is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. A sub is British slang for an advance on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you put forward a proposal or an entry for someone else to consider.

clue.text: Those queuing for free food rebel, and I worried

definitions.note: the definition names the people; the answer is the queue they form

indicators.note: worried letters are shaken about

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone in a food queue frets alongside a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation splits 'rebel' from 'and I', but both belong in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadline is a queue of people waiting for free food handed out by charity.

clue.text: Historian, one breaking down on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the answer only has to sound like the phrase

parts.note: an analyst breaks things down into parts

explanation.surface: A historian breaks down in tears during a radio interview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking down' suggests collapse; it means analysing. 'One' supplies the article: 'an analyst' said quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, year-by-year records, so is a historian.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvres and beer consumed by social worker, quietly downing two litres

parts.note: ants are social insects and workers
STILL = quietly, minus L and L
India pale ale

explanation.surface: Starters and beer are knocked back by a social worker who quietly downs two litres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is the crossword's ant, and 'quietly' is the fodder STILL rather than P; 'downing' means drinking up its two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters, the equivalent of hors d'oeuvres.

clue.text: Husband enters New Year drunk in whatever location

indicators.note: NEW YEAR is drunkenly rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
H = husband

explanation.surface: A husband staggers in drunk at New Year, anywhere at all.
explanation.walkthrough: New Year and drunk fit the party scene; 'New Year' is the fodder, and the H sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anywhere means in any place at all, whatever the location.

clue.text: Type of table sauce

definitions.meaning: the bedroom table with a mirror, where you get ready
the oil-and-vinegar kind poured over salad

explanation.surface: A question of which sauce belongs on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table sauce' reads as one thing, like ketchup; split it, and each half is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is completed by the answer as a compound noun; the second is a plain synonym for a salad sauce.

clue.text: Emotion drained, male is in gloomy state

indicators.note: is in means the next pieces sit inside the gloomy word

parts.note: dark means gloomy

indicators.note: drained means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of emotion

explanation.surface: A man spent of feeling sinks into depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' gives EN, and 'is in' puts EN and M inside DARK after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian country, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Those not scared about holding sparklers, maybe

indicators.note: as in 'about turn', the letters face the other way and are read right to left
the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: tho(SE NOT S)cared, read backwards

explanation.surface: People brave enough to hold lit sparklers on bonfire night.
explanation.walkthrough: The sparklers look like fireworks; they are gems, and 'maybe' warns that stones are only one kind of sparkler.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious stones sparkle, so they are sparklers by example.

clue.text: Jerk working as ship's doctor

parts.note: a jerk is a sudden surge
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An unpleasant man serving as the doctor on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as an insult; it is a sudden movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctor on a ship is traditionally called the ship's surgeon.

clue.text: Flops down, perhaps exhausted after endless work mending pipes?

indicators.note: after puts the outer letters behind the shortened plumbing word
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to plumb is to work as a plumber

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, keeping only the outer letters of perhaps

explanation.surface: A plumber collapses, worn out after an endless shift fixing pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims PLUMB to PLUM, and 'exhausted' leaves PS from perhaps, which comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump is to sit or drop down heavily and suddenly.

clue.text: Knot bow tie at last

parts.note: a bow of the head is a nod

indicators.note: at last means at the end, so only the final letter of TIE is used

parts.note: the last letter of TIE

explanation.surface: Finally knotting a bow tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow tie' looks like the neckwear; 'bow' is a nod of the head, and 'tie' only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knot, as in a knotty swelling on a stem or joint.

clue.text: Discovered idiot guards sick prisoner showing determination

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it, so the other letters sit inside
discovered means with its cover taken off, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a twerp is a silly or idiotic person
ill means sick
POW is the abbreviation for prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A fool found out keeping watch over an ailing inmate shows real resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' strips TWERP down to WER, which is split around ILL and POW.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is the strength of mind to carry on with something, so determination.

clue.text: Place to find spare tyre lying unused reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the answer only has to sound right

parts.note: land lying unused is waste

explanation.surface: A spare tyre is lying unused somewhere in the boot.
explanation.walkthrough: The car's spare tyre is the natural reading; a spare tyre is also a roll of fat round the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'spare tyre' of fat sits around the waist.

clue.text: Kitty ultimately raised for game

indicators.note: the word's ultimate, or last, letter is lifted one place higher in this down light

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money that players or members pay into

explanation.surface: The pot of money finally goes up for a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately raised' takes the final L of POOL and moves it up one square in the down entry, ahead of the last O, so POOL becomes the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team sport played on horseback with mallets and a ball.

clue.text: "Fatty" Arbuckle, originally flipping religious, shot bears

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of Arbuckle
bears means carries within, so the shot word holds the reversed letters

parts.note: a dose is a shot of medicine

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: PI is short for pious, religious

explanation.surface: Silent star Fatty Arbuckle, flipping from piety, was photographed.
explanation.walkthrough: Roscoe Arbuckle was a silent-film comedian nicknamed Fatty. 'flipping' turns PI into IP, and 'bears' puts it inside DOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means consisting of or relating to body fat, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Popular service, wrong to be cut back

indicators.note: EVIL loses its last letter

parts.note: a church service
EVIL, a wrong, with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A popular church service is wrongly scaled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular' leads to IN or POP; here it is the definition, in the informal sense of a massive hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something massive is hugely successful or popular, as in a massive hit.

clue.text: How to avoid a sunburnt back? Stay cool

definitions.text: How to avoid a sunburnt back
definitions.meaning: the literal reading: stay covered up

explanation.surface: Advice for a hot day: cover up to protect your back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay cool' looks like advice about heat, matching the sunburn; it is the idiom for not losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for not losing one's temper, paired with its literal sense of staying covered in the sun.
